children: Invitation Homes Inc.
INVH benefits from a scaled single-family rental portfolio in infill markets and multiple capital-light growth channels.

Builder partnerships and construction lending broaden its investment toolkit, while value-added services add incremental revenues. Share repurchases and asset sales support per-share returns, and liquidity remains ample.
INVH shares have rallied 9.3% over the past six months against the industry’s decline of 3.6%. Invitation Homes currently carries a Zacks Rank of 2 (Buy).
Factors That Make Invitation Homes Stock a Solid Pick
Infill Markets & Capital-Light Growth Channels:

Invitation Homes continues to target infill markets with high barriers to new housing supply while pursuing multiple avenues for growth. The company is expanding its growth through multiple channels, including buying homes from builders, developing new properties and providing construction financing. With a strong development pipeline and growing lending commitments, the company is creating additional opportunities for growth and fee-based income.
Technology Is Helping Revenues:

Invitation Homes continues to invest in technology and process enhancements to improve the resident experience and support margins. The ProCare application and value-added services such as Smart Home, internet bundle and the HVAC filter program are helping lift other property income. In second-quarter 2026, value-added service income increased about 9% year over year.
Balance Sheet Remains Strong:

Invitation Homes continues to recycle capital into accretive opportunities, selling 657 homes for about $309 million and repurchasing $100 million of stock in the second quarter of 2026. Liquidity stood at $1.55 billion, with net debt at 5.4X adjusted EBITDAre. In July, the company issued $500 million of 2032 notes to partially repay debt due in 2027, extending maturities and improving refinancing flexibility.
Dividend Support:

Invitation Homes continues to pair dividend payments with per-share earnings growth and repurchases. Core FFO per share increased 5% year over year to 51 cents in second-quarter 2026. Management raised the midpoint of full-year 2026 core FFO guidance to $1.95. The quarterly dividend remains 30 cents per share, supporting coverage, while the company continues capital recycling.
